title: Bit-Field Parameter Manipulation (Bitflag Obsession)
pattern: Using raw integers or bit fields to convey multiple independent boolean flags as method parameters, defining the meanings solely in comments.
why_bad: Swapping bit positions or passing incorrect values compiles cleanly but results in silent runtime state corruption. Callers must consult manual comments to know the bit flags.
detection: A function parameter is evaluated using bitwise operations against magic numbers or non-class constants.
counterexample: Using structured types, explicit Enums, or safe `bitflags` macros to represent parameters.
fix: Define a type-safe Bitflags enum or struct to restrict inputs to valid compile-checked values.
source: [Robert C. Martin series] Feathers, Michael C - WEWLC, p. 630-631 [630-631]; or Code Complete, Section 11.2 & 32.3 [803].
